waiting.title: We're Looking Forward to Seeing You!

items.question: 💸 Is the event free?
items.answer: Yes! All events are free and open to the public, but registration is required.

items.question: 🗣️ Will the sessions be bilingual?
items.answer: Yes, sessions will be available in English and French.

items.question: 👥 Who can attend?
items.answer: Everyone is welcome — individuals, families, and community organizations.

items.question: ⏰ What time should I arrive?
items.answer: Please arrive at least 30 minutes before the opening ceremony to allow time for registration and seating.

items.question: 🚗 Is parking available?
items.answer: Paid parking is available on site, and the venue is also accessible by public transit.

items.question: 🚍 How can I get there by public transit?
items.answer: The venue is accessible by OC Transpo bus routes and is near the Tremblay LRT station.

items.question: ♿ Is the venue accessible?
items.answer: Yes, the venue is fully accessible and equipped with elevators and accessible washrooms.

items.question: 🧠 Can I attend only part of the day?
items.answer: Yes, you are welcome to join at any time throughout the day's sessions.

items.question: 📧 Who can I contact for more information?
items.answer: For any questions, please contact the organizing team at ottawabmhcoalition@gmail.com

items.question: 💛 Can I volunteer or get involved?
items.answer: Yes, volunteers are always welcome! You can reach out to the organizing team for opportunities to help during the week.

about.title: About the Conference
about.description: Join Ottawa Black Mental Health Coalition and community partners for a week-long celebration centering Black mental wellness through powerful keynotes, panels, workshops, and community connection.
about.missionText: To break the stigma surrounding mental health in Black communities by fostering open dialogue, providing education, and connecting individuals with culturally competent mental health resources and support systems.
about.whyText: Black communities face unique mental health challenges, including systemic barriers to care, cultural stigma, and historical trauma. By addressing substance use and suicide openly, we can save lives and build resilient communities.
